comments.body: RE-VERIFIED 2026-08-10 (rad v0.11.0, dev build at 117b7329): confirmed on the current build. The re-propagation from `relay(stored)` on line 9 is reported as `error[RAD20000]: boom --> :4:10`, pointing at the `fail()` call inside the original catch line. The relay site appears nowhere in the output.

comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Fixed 2026-08-10 in 68bb2791 (branch rad-sprint1).

Went with "both sites", as the card proposed. `RadPanic` now carries a `RaiseSpan` recording where the panic fired when that differs from where the error was constructed; `NewRadPanic` sets it only when the error already had a span, so an ordinary first raise leaves it nil. `handlePanicRecovery` renders the two-span form via the existing `NewDiagnosticWithLabels` machinery - primary label "re-raised here", secondary "originally raised here".

The repro now renders:

    error[RAD20000]: boom
      --> :11:10
       |
     5 | stored = fail() catch:
       |          ------ originally raised here
    ...
    11 | result = relay(stored)
       |          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^ re-raised here

Multi-hop relays report the innermost re-arm point, which is where the panic actually fired.

No existing snapshot changed - origin and raise site coincide on a first raise, so single-span rendering is byte-identical. Regression test added to core/testing/snapshots/control_flow/catch.snap. Full suite green.

creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Split out of a_sBRDpFgU (2026-08-10). That card bundled a design question with a confirmed sub-bug; this is the sub-bug, which ships independently of whatever we decide about error defusal.

**Repro:**
fn fail():
    return error("boom")

stored = fail() catch:
    pass

fn relay(x):
    return x

result = relay(stored)  // crashes, and points at the fail() line, not relay()

**Root cause:** `core/errors.go:36-44` - `NewRadPanic` fills the span only when it is nil:

    unwrapped := err.RequireError(i, node)
    if unwrapped.Span == nil {
        unwrapped.Span = nodeSpanPtr(node)
    }

A stored error already carries the span from where it was first constructed, so re-panicking it at `core/type_fn.go:243-245` keeps the original attribution and the new call site is never recorded.

The intent to re-attribute already exists elsewhere: `core/type_fn.go:247-249` clears the span on the non-panicking propagate path, precisely so the next raise site can claim it. That just does not cover the panic path.

**Decision:** report the new site, the original site, or both. Both reads best - "raised at :3, re-raised at :9" - and it is the only version that does not throw away information the interpreter has at hand.

**Independent of the error-identity decision.** Whether or not `catch: pass` ends up defusing the value, blaming the wrong line is wrong.
title: Re-propagated errors are blamed on the original call site
